text:
vivek: quick follow-up on rollout metadata shape — want to avoid tight coupling between claim/owner and stability signals. proposing a minimal, dependency-aware shape that supports canaries and soft fallbacks.

elena: SGTM. can you paste the minimal schema idea?

vivek: sure, rough sketch:```json
{
  "claimed_by": "team/model-owner",
  "stability_score": 87,           // 0-100 auto/heuristic score
  "soft_expiry": "2025-05-01T12:00:00Z",
  "provenance": [{ "actor": "ci/deploy", "reason": "canary", "ts": "2025-04-01T18:00:00Z" }],
  "dependencies": [ "base-model:v2", "quant:8bit" ],
  "fallback_policy_ref": "policies/fallbacks/v1"
}
```

sam: quick Q — who sets soft_expiry in practice? control plane or client?

vivek: control plane writes soft_expiry during rollout. clients can probe and request rebind before expiry; fallback kicks in after grace window.

grace: do we need a provenance chain strong enough to detect tenant overrides? worried about noisy overrides stomping signals.

vivek: include provenance entries but keep them coarse: actor, reason, ts, trust_level. sanitize at ingest so tenants can't forge system signals.

elena: i like stability_score numeric. how do we compute it?

sam: rolling metrics: p95 latency regression, error-rate delta, plus eval harness results. keep formula pluggable.

vivek: also suggest adding an optional field "retirement_eta" for planned deprecation (iso8601) and "migration_hint" text.

elena: nit: rename "owner" -> "claimed_by" to avoid implying permanent lock. good to surface claimed_by in telemetry.

vivek: agreed. changed. also added "dependencies" so a control-plane can reason: if quant variant fails, fallback to base-model.

grace: operational ask: can we run a canary that sets TTL=1h and force-fallback to older variant if regressions > 2%?

sam: yes — that should be an ops policy (fallback_policy_ref resolves to that behavior). schema just stores the pointer.

vivek: thinking about API ergonomics: SDK should expose simple helpers: bind(), unbind(), claim_tentative(), probe_stability(). low-level patch for ops.

elena: add example curl to update claimed_by and provenance?

vivek: yep:```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://api.redwood.ai/rollouts/123/metadata" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"claimed_by":"team/model-owner","provenance":[{"actor":"ci/deploy","reason":"canary","ts":"2025-04-01T18:00:00Z"}]}'
```

ops-bot: @deploy-bot pinned metadata schema v0.3 applied to staging :white_check_mark:

grace: follow-up: we should prevent low-trust actors from lowering stability_score directly. sanitize rules?

vivek: yes — only system actors or high-trust service accounts can set stability_score. others can attach observed metrics which the control plane folds into the score.

elena: final suggestion: add "signal_sources" list to record which subsystems contributed (a11y, latency-monitor, eval-harness). helps debugging.

vivek: good call. adding that. final-ish shape will include claimed_by, stability_score, soft_expiry, provenance, dependencies, fallback_policy_ref, retirement_eta, signal_sources.

vivek: action items: 1) elena update onboarding docs with examples, 2) sam run 24h canary in prod tomorrow, 3) grace implement provenance sanitizer + tests, 4) ops add fallback policy for >2% regression.

elena: i'll take docs.

sam: i'll own canary infra.

grace: i'll write sanitizer tests.

vivek: thanks all — i'll file a short RFC follow-up with the final JSON examples and link to the canary checklist. :rocket:
